title: Span handoff handshake: instrumentation adapter for graceful cross-process span handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We still lose trace continuity when requests hop across transports with different propagation semantics (WebSocket upgrades, serverless invoke->worker queue->worker, and some legacy gRPC proxies). Existing OTEL header propagation covers most HTTP flows but is lossy for: 1) long-lived socket upgrades where the initial upgrade carries context but subsequent frames are not annotated, 2) small worker messages (SQS/Kafka) where serializers strip unknown headers, and 3) ephemeral serverless cold starts where the initial HTTP carrier is absent. Goal: design and ship a compact, backwards-compatible 'span handoff handshake' adapter that provides a minimal encoded handshake in carriers and SDK middleware so span parentage can be reconstructed with high fidelity and minimal overhead.
design_summary: We will introduce a thin, optional handshake header (X-RW-Span-HH) that embeds a compact span reference envelope (trace_id, parent_id_hint, sampling_flag, short sequence id, and TTL) using base64url + zlib-lite compression for fringe cases. SDK middleware will: (a) emit the handshake on upgrade or enqueue events, (b) listen for handshake on inbound frames/messages, (c) attempt a best-effort span reconstruction (enriching existing OTEL context when present), and (d) fall back to existing propagation if handshake absent. The adapter will be implemented as middleware in Node/Python/Go SDKs and as a runtime-level filter for websocket/gRPC proxies.
api_and_contracts: Header name: X-RW-Span-HH (case-insensitive). Encoding: base64url of a zlib-lite compressed TLV: {v:1, t:trace_id(16B hex), p:parent_id(8B hex, optional), s:seq(4B), f:flags(1B), ttl_seconds}. Max uncompressed size: 48 bytes. Header size budget: target 256 bytes, hard cap 1024 bytes. Public SDKs will expose middleware helpers: .emitSpanHandshake(), .consumeSpanHandshake(), and a configuration flag `handshake_enabled` (default: false). The runtime filter will translate the header to internal carrier for inter-service RPC to avoid header stripping.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Pros: higher trace continuity across non-HTTP carriers, low reconstruction logic, opt-in to control adoption. Cons: additional header surface (privacy/POI), slight CPU for compression/decompression, risk of header stripping by intermediaries, and complexity in ensuring backward compatibility with OTEL. Risk mitigations: opt-in flag, sampling-aware emission, max header size, and graceful fallback to OTEL headers. Security: header contains no PII and only identifiers; we'll sign the envelope with HMAC when feature is enabled in Private deployments (KMS-backed key) — opt-in and separate rollout.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (this ticket): spec + middleware prototype (Node + Python) + runtime websocket filter + unit/integration tests. Create a GitHub PR for runtime and SDKs. Phase 2: add Go SDK and worker queue adapters, end-to-end perf tests, and Canary rollout flag. Phase 3: opt-in HMAC signing for Private customers and add dashboarding metrics for handshake success/failure rates.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end trace continuity verified across websocket upgrade -> frames -> backend with integration test harness (<=1% lost parent links on 10k trace sample)
Worker queue flow (HTTP enqueue -> SQS message -> worker) reconstructs parent span in 99.5% cases in integration tests
Header size < 512 bytes for 99.9% of emitted handshakes in synthetic workload
SDKs provide middleware helpers and have unit tests covering emit/consume paths
Feature is behind a runtime flag and can be rolled back without client SDK changes (middleware yields no-op when disabled)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime + Node prototype behind runtime flag (0%). 2) Internal canary: 5% of internal traffic for 2 weeks (monitor handshake_success_rate and latency). 3) Gradual ramp to 20% over two weeks if no regressions. 4) Add Python/Go SDK support and enable for customer beta group. 5) Evaluate HMAC signing as separate gated rollout for Private customers.
monitoring_and_metrics: New metrics: handshake_emitted_total, handshake_consumed_total, handshake_reconstruct_success_total, handshake_decode_error_total, handshake_header_size_histogram. Add dashboards: handshake health panel (success rate by service/region), trace continuity SLI (percent traces with reconstructed parent), and p99 end-to-end latency impact panel.
qa_plan: Unit tests in SDKs; integration tests with websocket proxy + runtime e2e harness; fault injection tests (strip header, corrupted payload, truncated header); load test at 1000 rps for handshake generation to verify CPU cost < 2% overhead per node.
security_notes: Header contains only identifiers; no user tokens. For Private customers that opt-in to signed handshakes, use KMS to store signing keys and rotate quarterly. Threat model doc referenced in docs_links. Security review requested for phase 2 (signing): set security_review_required = true in parent ticket.
